office: the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA)

routes.label: in person at a NIRA office, for biometrics; collected at the place of residence

note: NIRA's 2025 registration and renewal drive, as Pulse Uganda reported it: a child's new registration (under 18) is free, a renewal is free, a lost card costs Shs 50,000 to replace and a change of details Shs 200,000 (replacements and changes not modelled). An adult's first registration needs a local leader's letter or a citizenship certificate; its fee isn't stated, so it's null. The card's term and the time aren't stated either. NIRA's own site serves its pages only through a script this session couldn't run.

sources.title: Pulse Uganda, When and how to renew your Ugandan national ID (June 2025)
sources.said: There are no fees for renewing your National ID. ... A fee of Shs 50,000 applies for replacing a lost ID, and Shs 200,000 applies for correcting or changing personal details. ... For children under 18, registration is free, provided a parent or blood relative’s National ID is presented. Adults registering for the first time will need additional documentation such as a local leader’s letter or a citizenship certificate from the Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control.
